strategy.name: Short nano caps after a priced offering
strategy.summary: When a company with under $50M public float files a final prospectus (424B4/424B5), short it at the first close after the filing, hedge with an equal long position in IWM, and cover after 20 trading days or if the price doubles.
strategy.hypothesis: Priced offerings in the smallest companies are followed by continued selling: new shares and warrants hit the market, and these issuers often raise again. The Edge Lab measured -13.7% vs ordinary days over 20 trading days (t=-5.7) in Oct 2023 - Aug 2026.

borrow_check.note: Today's borrow for nano caps that priced an offering in the last 6 months of period B. Fees right at an offering are likely higher, so treat these as a lower bound.

key_finding.text: The drift is real before frictions: the average short returned +4.7% per trade out-of-sample (median +8.7%) and +8.2% in the discovery period. The biggest single cost is 'Borrow fee (75%/yr)' (5.8% per trade). With every assumed friction the strategy loses money, so it is not tradable as specified. It loses money even with free borrow (out-of-sample) and breaks even at an average borrow fee of about 76%/yr (discovery period). Today's IBKR file shows a median fee of 7%/yr for recent nano-cap issuers (36% at the 75th percentile), with 97% borrowable, so the 75% assumption may be pessimistic. But cheaper borrow alone would not rescue it: the out-of-sample period fails on spread, squeeze stops, recalls and unborrowable names even at zero borrow. The edge looks strongest in the most recent years, which could be a regime change (more toxic offerings since 2023) or luck. Only fresh data can tell.

verdict.headline: Not ready for real money
verdict.detail: Fails 8 research gate(s): Out-of-sample Sharpe, Out-of-sample return after costs, Deflated Sharpe (A), Max drawdown, Survives worst-case stress (A), Robust to random borrow luck (A), Survives limited borrow (A), Capacity at $100k. Fix or abandon before paper trading.

not_modeled: Short squeezes beyond the daily close (intraday spikes can trigger margin calls before the stop).
Borrow recalls and buy-ins: lenders can take shares back at any time.
Hard-to-borrow fees that change daily and can exceed 200%/yr right after an offering.
Locate failures at the moment of entry; the first close after an offering is when demand to short peaks.
Margin: shorts need 150%+ collateral under Reg T, and brokers raise requirements on volatile nano caps.
Taxes: every trade is short-term; short dividends and fees are ordinary expenses.

assumptions: Entry at the close 1 trading day(s) after the first close a trader could act on after EDGAR acceptance (Rule 201 often blocks shorting into the day-0 drop).
Hold 20 trading days; cover if the close is 40% above entry, filled 5% worse.
Position size 3% of equity, at most 5% of the 20-day median dollar volume; max 25 positions, total shorts at most 100% of equity.
Skip stocks under $1.00 (unadjusted) or with under $200,000/day median volume before entry.
Round-trip spread and slippage 3.0%; borrow 75%/yr on the short notional.
30% of trades randomly unborrowable; 2%/day chance of a recall, covered 2% worse.
If price data ends (delisting or halt), cover at the last price +10%: no credit for the delisting.
Each short is hedged with an equal long position in IWM (about 0.04% round trip).
Size from SEC public float measured before each period (Q2 2020 for A, Q2 2023 for B).
Prices: Yahoo adjusted closes; delisted names without data are excluded and counted under coverage.
Risk-free rate is zero and short proceeds earn no interest (conservative; brokers pay some rebate on large accounts).
